title: Utah football’s starting offensive tackle out for season with lower-leg injury
text:
Utah football loses Kelvin Obot to season-ending injury 
 Utah football’s starting offensive tackle out for season with lower-leg injury
 Kelvin Obot is a former five-star recruit from the 2026 recruiting class. 
 (Trent Nelson | The Salt Lake Tribune) The Moment of Loudness as Utah hosts Houston, NCAA football at Rice-Eccles Stadium in Salt Lake City on Saturday, Oct. 24, 2026.
 By  Jason Batacao  | Nov. 2, 2026, 12:40 p.m. | Updated: 1:56 p.m. Comment
 Add as Preferred Source
 Utah offensive tackle Kelvin Obot is out for the season with a lower-leg injury, head coach Morgan Scalley said Monday.
 “By way of announcement on the injury front, Kelvin Obot is out for the season,” Scalley said. “Lower-leg deal. Not getting into the specifics there, but he’ll be done for the year.” 
 Obot left Utah’s win over Colorado on Oct. 17 after being rolled up on during a run by Wayshawn Parker. Obot quickly emerged as the starter at the position after rotating behind right tackles Cedric Jefferson and Keith Olson to start the year.
 Jefferson started in Obot’s place in the Utes’ blowout win over Cincinnati this weekend. Now Utah will turn its attention to a top-10 matchup at home against in-state rival BYU.
 “We’ve got BYU coming up, huge matchup,” Scalley said. “I believe it’s the first time that we’ve both been in the top 10 going up against each other. It’s awesome, awesome for the state. Big rivalry game. Kalani, respect the heck out of him.”
